user.title: Battery Pool
user.description: Create a pool, then use Configure to add batteries.

data_description.name: A name of your choice for the group of battery systems, e.g. “Home storage”. Add individual battery systems afterwards through Configure.

add_battery.title: Add battery system
add_battery.description: Save mappings and intermediate configurations independently of other battery systems. Checks for actual power commands run during operation. Setpoint entities are controlled, device maxima are only read, and additional pool limits still apply.

data_description.name: A name of your choice, unique within this pool, e.g. “Garage battery”. This identifies one battery system, rather than the whole pool.
data_description.capacity_kwh: Usable energy capacity of this battery system according to its manufacturer or configuration, e.g. 5.12 kWh. Used to weight the pool state of charge. Enter a number greater than 0, rather than power in W or a sensor.
data_description.soc_entity: Select the sensor reporting this battery system’s current state of charge (SOC) as a number from 0 to 100 in %, e.g. sensor.garage_battery_soc. Do not select a voltage, energy, or pool sensor.
data_description.power_entity: Select the sensor measuring this battery system’s current AC charging/discharging power in watts, e.g. sensor.garage_battery_ac_power. Do not select an energy meter (kWh), household consumption, grid connection, or setpoint. Values in kW must first be converted to W.
data_description.command_entity: Signed mode only: select the number or input_number for the CURRENT power request in W, using positive/negative values for the two directions and zero to stop. Do not select maximum charge or discharge power.
data_description.min_soc: The planner does not request further discharge below this state of charge, e.g. 20 % as a reserve. Enter 0–100, less than the upper charge limit. This does not change a device setting.
data_description.max_soc: The planner does not request further charging at or above this state of charge, e.g. 90 %. Enter 0–100, greater than the lower discharge limit. This does not change a device setting.
data_description.max_charge_w: Additional per-battery software limit; default 300 W, greater than zero. The current charge request cannot exceed this limit OR the optionally linked device maximum. This is neither an entity selection nor a current charge request.
data_description.max_discharge_w: Additional per-battery software limit; default 300 W, greater than zero. The current discharge request cannot exceed this limit OR the optionally linked device maximum. This is neither an entity selection nor a current discharge request.
data_description.positive_discharge: Measured AC power convention: on = positive discharge, negative charge; off = reversed. In signed mode the combined command must use the same convention. Separate charge/discharge requests are always positive magnitudes.
data_description.adapter_confirmed: Confirm that the selected controls send current power requests, the device remote-control mode is correct, and a device-side watchdog stops power if commands cease. Both separate setpoints must stop their direction at zero; a combined signed setpoint must stop at zero and support both signs. An input_number needs a real device bridge. Maximum-power controls alone are insufficient. If a mode entity is assigned, its three mapped options must activate the correct directions or a true idle state. General remote-control prerequisites must already be configured correctly.
data_description.command_mode: Separate setpoints: one entity each for the current requested charge and discharge power, both positive watts. This fits devices with four controls (two requests and two maxima). Signed: one combined entity for both directions. Only the setpoint fields for the selected mode are used.
data_description.charge_command_entity: Separate mode: select the control for the CURRENT requested charging power, e.g. “Set charging power”. Positive values request charging; zero stops the charge request. Do not select “Maximum charging power”. The discharge request is explicitly zeroed before any charge command.
data_description.discharge_command_entity: Separate mode: select the control for the CURRENT requested discharging power, e.g. “Set discharging power”. Positive values request discharge; zero stops the discharge request. Do not select “Maximum discharging power”. The charge request is explicitly zeroed before any discharge command.
data_description.max_charge_entity: Optionally select the separate “Maximum charging power” control or sensor in W. Its current value is read as an additional ceiling; the pool never writes to it. It is not a charge request. Zero disables charging; invalid or stale readings stop the pool. If omitted, the additional pool limit applies.
data_description.max_discharge_entity: Optionally select the separate “Maximum discharging power” control or sensor in W. Its current value is read as an additional ceiling; the pool never writes to it. It is not a discharge request. Zero disables discharge; invalid or stale readings stop the pool. If omitted, the additional pool limit applies.
data_description.power_unit_w_confirmed: Confirm only when device documentation states that the selected setpoint and maximum-power entities use watts but Home Assistant displays no unit. Missing units on these controls are then accepted. A, kW and % are not converted and remain invalid. Measurement sensors still require the correct units.
data_description.mode_entity: If the device additionally determines power direction through a mode, select its select or input_select entity, e.g. “Forced mode”. In the next step map its actual options for charge, discharge and idle. Do not use the general user mode selecting manual, automatic or trading operation. If omitted, device modes are left unchanged. Existing options are suggestions; values can also be entered manually while entities are offline.

edit_battery.description: Edit the saved entities, capacity, and limits of this battery system.

remove_battery.title: Select battery

data_description.battery: Select one of the battery systems already saved in this pool by its name.

remove_battery.description: Only removes the saved mapping from this pool. The device and its Home Assistant entities are retained. Confirm removal in the next step.

control_settings.title: Control mode
control_settings.description: Verify in simulation first. Switching off, invalid readings, and unloading the integration request 0 W for every confirmed adapter. During network or device failure only a device-side watchdog can guarantee stopping.

data.grid_confirmed: Verified: positive grid import and negative export

data_description.control_mode: External request: set the pool number entity, positive to discharge and negative to charge. Refresh at least every 60 seconds or the pool stops. Self-consumption: balance import/export using the grid sensor. Both modes require the pool switch to be on.
data_description.live_control: Off by default: simulation only, no device power commands. Enable only after verifying every adapter. The pool still starts switched off and requires its switch to be activated. Restarting or changing options switches the pool off again.
data_description.grid_power_entity: Self-consumption only: sensor at the shared grid connection measuring the whole home including all pool batteries. Unit W, positive = import, negative = export. Do not select PV generation, household consumption excluding batteries, or an individual battery sensor.
data_description.grid_confirmed: For self-consumption, verify that grid import is positive and export is negative in W. An incorrect convention can amplify the imbalance. All battery sensors must measure the same AC side of this grid connection.
data_description.grid_target_w: Default 20 W residual grid import rather than exact zero export. A small positive margin reduces oscillation near zero. Only used in self-consumption mode.

battery_modes.title: Map device modes
battery_modes.description: Enter the charging, discharging and idle options for {entity}. Existing options are suggestions. Saving does not check plausibility, allowing intermediate migration states. Entity and option checks still apply before real device commands.

data_description.charge_mode: Option activating charging, e.g. charge. Not a general user mode such as manual.
data_description.idle_mode: A true idle option, e.g. standby. Requested at 0 W, on faults, when the pool is switched off and on unload. Do not select an automatic mode which independently charges or discharges.

error.invalid_number: Enter a finite number within the permitted range.
